description.narrative:
Diakonia, en av Sidas ramorganisationer, har till Sida inkommit med en ansökan om att Sida, tillsammans med fem givare, bidrar till insatsen " Common Gender Fund and its Strategic Plan 2019-2023" i Burkina Faso 2019-2023. Insatsen syftar till att bidra att stärka kvinnors och flickors sociala, ekonomiska, politiska rättigheter genom diverse åtgärder för att på så sätt minska ojämställdhet mellan könen på nationell nivå. Sida har tidigare bidragit med stöd till Common Gender Fund under perioden 2012-2014 och 2016-2018.
Diakonia kommer att genomföra stödet tillsammans med lokala icke-statliga organisationer och myndigheter. Insatsens totala budget är 89 miljoner kronor, varav Sida bidrar med 15 miljoner kronor. Övriga givare (Danmark, Schweiz, UNFPA, UNICEF) kommer att bidra med cirka 27 miljoner kronor. Cirka 73 procent av budgeten kommer att vidareförmedlas till tredje part.

Diakonia, one of Sida's framework organizations, has submitted an application to Sida to jointly finance the intervention "the Common Gender Fund and its Strategic Plan 2019-2023” together with four other donors during the period 2019-2023. The intervention aims to contribute to the implementation of relevant and effective actions to strengthen women's and girls' social, economic, political rights through actions to promote the abandonment of GBV, promotion of economic and political empowerment, strengthening gender mainstreaming, involvement of women and youth in the management of security issues, in order to to reduce gender inequalities at the national level. Sida has previously contributed to the Common Gender Fund in 2012-2014 and 2016-2018.
Diakonia will implement the intervention together with local CSOs and Government authorities. The total budget is 89 Million SEK out of which Sida will contribute with 15 million SEK. Other donors (Denmark, Switzerland, UNFPA, UNICEF) will contribute with approximately 27 million SEK. Approximately 73 % of the intervention budget will be forwarded from Diakonia to third parties.

description.narrative:
The overall technical and financial execution rates for projects from 2022 to June 30, 2023 are 78% and 68.66% respectively for the implementing partners. The budget execution rate as at June 30 for the 2023 budget is 70.97%. The consolidated budget execution rate for 2019-30/6/2023 is is 69.98%.
In the absence of a annual report (expected on 2024-03-31), the impact of the intervention can be sought in various testimonials that have been provided by the cooperation partner.
Axis 1: Strengthening actions to promote the abandonment of gender based violence (GBV)
Under this axis, several examples can be highlighted. Through the FCGs support to the Centre Delwende de Sakoula, for women (and men) accused of witchcraft, managed to reintegrate 6 of its pensioners in their communities of origin during 2023.
In Koudougou the FCG has been engaged in the promotion of income-generating activities (IGAs). To counter the backlash from some of the male members of the community, the cooperation partner (FWY) has organized awarness raising activities and engaged in dialogue with the men. Community dialogues were carried out in the village with men on the denial of resources and the economic empowerment of women. Changes in behavior have been observed among many men who now accept that their wives engage in IGAs. A testimonial from one beneficiary affirms that it is thanks to the awareness raising carried out by the project and particularly the community dialogue or with the testimony of certain men on the well-being and development of family members thanks to the IGAs carried out by their wives that her husband became aware and accepted that she exercised an IGA. I am now a traveling trader. I sell sandwiches. At the beginning he set me hours not to exceed. This is no longer relevant, now I can sell without fear of being questioned. This brings me joy because I help financially support the needs of my children and the household. I am fulfilled because I am able to please myself.
Axis 2: Economic and political empowerment of women and young people
In the commune of Niou, the cooperation partner (ADC-Delwénde) has worked extensively on women's access to land. A testomony from a beneficary informs us that: awareness raising on rights and duties and training on female leadership and local development have made us realize that we can have access to land for our activities. Thus, we approached the President of the Special Delegation who translated our request to the council. The Special Delegation took a decision which authorizes us to occupy a plot of 1000m2 for the creation of a literacy room and an IGA training center."
In the commune of Toéghin, the FCG has worked on reinforcing the skills and capacities of women who are members of the local government (Special Delegations), including through literacy training and strengthening of advocay skills. The of the association of women weavers of Toéghin and member of the special delegation states: I had a concern that I wanted to ask the special delegation council but I was afraid. We are 2 women among the 22 members. Plus I'm illiterate. But since the training I received, during the counseling courses, I took my courage and raised the problem of the abandonment of the shops in the Toéghin market, and my concern was taken into account because the shops were withdrawn and reallocated to new tenants. Since then, I have participated in the debates during the council".
Axis 3: Strengthening gender mainstreaming in the development and monitoring of public policies, projects and programs by institutions and CSOs
N/A as Axis 3 is not part of the activities for this period.
Axis 4: Involvement of women and youth in the management of security issues
Through its partner Plate-forme d'Actions à la Sécurisation des Ménages Pastoraux (PASMEP), the FCG work towards better inclusion of women and girls in the management of pastoralist conflicts, including through the training of women in conflict management and mediation.
One beneficiary states: since the security crisis that our country is experiencing, fear reigns in our community (Peulh) and our commune suffers enormously. The peace-seeking project which involves young leaders, women and IDPs, conflict prevention and management has already borne fruit. I take the direct example of the contribution of training on leadership which allowed us to be better equipped to move towards the resolution of conflicts by organizing meetings between Fulani and Kassena communities for the settlement of a land dispute which dated 10 years ago, under the good offices of the President of the special delegation of Po. There have also been settlements of conflicts between two communities, farmers and breeders by indicating appropriate passages of herds to also avoid conflicts between them. These two examples give me the idea that PASMEP and its donor FCG must continue the activities
It is clear that the FCG is able to concrete results on an individual basis. It is more difficult to draw any conclusions on whether the FCG has a systemic impact on the issue of gender equality in Burkina Faso. This is mainly due to the difficulty of the FCG to measure and report its impact against indicators, despite these existing. The embassy has contionusly raised the importance of reporting on an impact level and not only on output level and some improvements can be noted over the years. Both the annual report 2023, as well as the final evaluation of the FCG Strategic Plan 2019-2023 will be highly informative with regards to the impact of the FCG.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
